definitions.definition: Xn=ℝ^n with the standard orthonormal coordinates indexed by j=1,…,n, its Euclidean norm and inner product, and its standard topology.

Ym=ℝ^m with its standard Euclidean norm |y|=sqrt(Σ_k y_k²) and real inner product ⟨y,z⟩=Σ_k y_k z_k; k runs from 1 to m. All inner products and vector norms below use the corresponding standard real Euclidean structures.
Ω={(x,t)∈Xn×ℝ : t>0}. Positive-time differentiation means ordinary differentiation in this open domain, with no assertion at t=0.
ũ(x,t)=u(x,t) when t>0 and ũ(x,t)=q when t≤0. This only specifies a total representation of u; no regularity at nonpositive times is asserted.

For real normed spaces A,B, a function f:A→B, a point z∈A and a direction v∈A, write D_v f(z)=Df(z)[v]=fderiv ℝ f z v. Here Df(z) is the continuous linear Fréchet derivative when it exists, and the total fderiv convention gives the zero continuous linear map otherwise. This notation alone asserts no differentiability.

b_std is the standard orthonormal basis; its jth vector, written b_j for j=1,…,n, has jth coordinate 1 and other coordinates 0. Fin n indices 0,…,n−1 are an equivalent relabeling with the same Euclidean structures and volume.

definitions.type: family of constant spatial directions in Xn×ℝ

definitions.definition: On Ω set u_t=D_T ũ, u_tt=D_T(D_T ũ), ∂_{x_j}u=D_{S_j}ũ, ∂_{x_jx_j}u=D_{S_j}(D_{S_j}ũ), and ∂_{x_j}u_t=D_{S_j}(D_T ũ). For any scalar or vector field h on Ω use the same total extension convention (arbitrary off Ω) and write ∂_t h=D_T h and ∂_{x_j}h=D_{S_j}h on Ω. These are derivatives of the original germs wherever differentiable. Δ_xu=Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u componentwise, and |D_xu|²=Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|² is the Frobenius square.

definitions.definition: For (x,t)∈Ω, e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². The normalization contains no factor 1/2. When a total time function is needed extend e by zero at t≤0.

argument.text: Fix x0 and tau>0, and introduce Vfield,Wfield,Afield,Bfield as declared. H001 implies ũ is smooth on the open Ω. M008 gives a smooth Fréchet derivative field there. Its evaluation at each constant direction is smooth, because evaluation at a fixed vector is continuous linear. Repeating M008 and fixed-vector evaluation shows that Vfield,Wfield,Afield,Bfield and the spatial derivatives of Vfield are smooth on Ω. In particular all are differentiable at (x0,tau). The affine restrictions in time and space are smooth and have derivatives obtained by evaluation in T and S_j by the chain rule. All such curves stay inside Ω near their positive-time base points.

produces.statement: ũ and all the declared derivative fields are smooth on Ω; time-curve derivatives of Vfield and Wfield are D_T Vfield and D_T Wfield, and spatial directional derivatives are their D_{S_j} derivatives at every positive-time point. In particular ũ is C² at (x0,tau).

argument.text: Define Lfield as declared. For every coordinate j, differentiating evaluation at a constant vector gives D_T Wfield_j=(D_T Lfield)[S_j], since Wfield_j=Lfield[S_j]; there is no derivative of the fixed S_j. Similarly D_{S_j}Vfield=(D_{S_j}Lfield)[T]. Apply M007 to ũ at (x0,tau), using F001's C² regularity. Symmetry of its second derivative makes these expressions equal. Thus the mixed derivative needed in the energy calculation is D_T Wfield_j=D_{S_j}Vfield at (x0,tau).

Apply M005 to the time curve r↦Vfield(x0,r) at tau, whose derivative is Afield(x0,tau), and for each j to r↦Wfield_j(x0,r), whose derivative is D_T Wfield_j(x0,tau). These derivatives follow from F001 and the directional definitions. Differentiate the finite sum in D011 and substitute F002. This yields ∂_t e(x0,tau)=2⟨Vfield,Afield⟩(x0,tau)+2Σ_j⟨Wfield_j,D_{S_j}Vfield⟩(x0,tau).

For each j apply M006 on Xn×ℝ to f=Vfield, g=Wfield_j, direction S_j at (x0,tau). Both functions are differentiable there by F001. D012 identifies their inner product with g_j on the positive-time neighborhood, and Bfield_j=D_{S_j}Wfield_j. The product rule gives ∂_{x_j}g_j(x0,tau)=⟨Vfield(x0,tau),Bfield_j(x0,tau)⟩+⟨D_{S_j}Vfield(x0,tau),Wfield_j(x0,tau)⟩.

Subtract twice the finite sum of F004 from F003. Symmetry of the real inner product cancels the terms containing D_{S_j}Vfield. Bilinearity combines the remaining terms into 2⟨Vfield,Afield-Σ_j Bfield_j⟩(x0,tau). The identifications in the declarations make this 2⟨u_t,u_tt-Σ_j∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩(x0,tau), which is zero by the second clause of N001. Hence ∂_t e=2Σ_j∂_{x_j}g_j at this point, with exactly the factor 2. Universal introduction over arbitrary x0 and positive tau proves the claimed output.
